abFundingBody: iHYPE is funded entirely by advertising, the same way terrestrial radio has always worked — and those ads are restricted to music-related sources only, forever. No user-data resale funds this platform, and no ticket revenue is ever touched.
abHeroBody: iHYPE exists because fans, not fees, should decide who rises. We give independent artists, venues, and DJs a platform that doesn't take a cut — but none of it means anything without fans showing up to hype, buy, and spread the word. No platform fee on tickets. No algorithmic pay-to-play. Built and governed by the community it serves.
abTeamBody: iHYPE is built by a small team of musicians, developers, and community organizers who got tired of watching independent venues close and independent artists lose income to platform fees. We are not venture-backed. We do not have a growth-at-all-costs mandate.
abTl1B: iHYPE incorporated as a not-for-profit organization in Portland, Maine. The founding charter locked in 0% platform fees and the 70/20/10 revenue split.
abTl2B: The iHYPE design system and community charter were published openly. The revenue split, governance model, and founding principles are locked in the charter.
abTl3B: Beta access opened to artists, venues, and promoters in the Portland area. First shows went live on the platform.
abTl4B: Fan beta access opened nationally. Audio-only radio shows and live DJ sets went live. iHYPE has never hosted video and never will.

askDescVal:
iHYPE is live music built on one rule: the platform takes nothing from ticket sales.

Every ticket splits 70% to the artist, 20% to the venue, 10% to a promoter pool shared by everyone who helped spread the word — locked in our founding charter. No service fees, no processing markup beyond the unavoidable cost of accepting a card.

Listen to the radio, hype the artists you believe in before anyone else has heard of them, and buy tickets at face value — direct.

iHYPE is funded by music-only advertising, the same way terrestrial radio always has been. No data sales. No streaming cuts. No middlemen.
askKeywordsVal: live music, concert tickets, local artists, indie music, radio, ticketing, venue, DJ, no fees, discover music
askPromoVal: Now in closed beta in Portland, ME. Discover local artists, buy tickets at face value, and hype the shows you believe in — every ticket splits 70/20/10, forever.

chHeroBody: iHYPE was incorporated with a single non-negotiable structural commitment: the platform takes nothing from ticket sales. Not a policy. A constraint. Changing it would require dissolving the company.
chLockedB: The 70/20/10 split is a condition of incorporation. Changing it would require dissolving the company and re-incorporating under a different structure. No board vote, no shareholder approval, no acquisition clause overrides it.
chMoneyB: iHYPE is funded entirely by advertising, the same way terrestrial radio has always worked — and those ads are restricted to music-related sources only, forever. None of it touches the ticket split. Tickets are processed directly through Stripe; the card-processing fee (2.9% + $0.30; AMEX 3.5% + $0.30) is the only charge above face value, passed through at cost.
chPromB: The 10% promoter pool is distributed to everyone who shared a referral link that contributed to ticket sales for an event. There's no separate promoter account — any Fan, Artist, DJ, or Venue earns from the links they already share.
chPullquote: This is not a pricing strategy. It is a constraint. We built the business model around it, not the other way around.
chRealB: A charter is just a promise on paper until a fan buys a ticket. Every dollar that hits this split exists because someone hyped an artist, showed up, and paid face value instead of going through a scalper. Artists write the songs, venues open the doors — but fans are the ones who make the 70/20/10 mean anything at all.

lpArtistBandP: iHYPE is a nonprofit. The 70% to you is enshrined in the charter, legally, before a single ticket sells. No agent required.
lpArtistsWritep: Artists write the songs. DJs spin the sets. Venues open the doors. None of it happens without fans showing up first. That's the part you play.

lpHeroSub: Local music is broken — pay-to-play discovery, tickets marked up 30%+, artists who never see who actually showed up. Fans are the fix. Every hype you cast, every ticket you buy direct, every friend you bring — that's what keeps the scene alive. iHYPE just makes it count.
lpMechanicsSub: Every step moves value from the middlemen back to artists and the fans who found them first.
lpModelBody: The promoter's 10% is its own dedicated slice — iHYPE takes 0%. The only charge above face value is the card-processing fee (Stripe 2.9% + $0.30; AMEX 3.5% + $0.30), passed through at cost.
lpNoSpam: No spam. Small waves. Artists + fans first.

lpStep1H: Back the artists you believe in
lpStep1P: A weekly flame budget lets you hype any artist, track, or show. The HYPE chart rises in real time.
lpStep2P: Every event publishes a split that can never change after sale. You see exactly where your money goes.
lpStep3H: Spread the word, earn a cut
lpStep3P: Share any event with your referral link. Earn up to 10% of the gate you drove — from the dedicated promoter slice, never the artist's.
lpThing1P: Your HYPE is a real vote, not a like. When you back an artist early, venues and other fans actually see it — that's how someone gets discovered instead of paying to be seen.
lpThing2P: Face value, no scalper markup. Buying direct is what actually pays the artist 70% and the room 20% — not a platform fee that never reaches either of them.
lpThing3P: Share a show with your link. If a ticket sells because you spread the word, you earn a real cut of the 10% promoter pool — never the artist's share.
lpWhatYouDoH2: Three small things. One big difference for the scene.

pkBoilerplateBody: iHYPE is a not-for-profit live music platform built around a single idea: fans, not fees, should decide who rises. Every ticket splits 70% to the artist, 20% to the venue, and 10% to a promoter pool shared by whoever helped sell it — locked in iHYPE's charter and unchangeable without dissolving and re-incorporating the company. The platform takes nothing from ticket sales; it's funded entirely by music-related advertising, the same way terrestrial radio has always worked. Founded in Portland, Maine in January 2026, iHYPE is run by two people and AI automation.
pkFactV3: HYPE — a real fan vote, not a like button
pkFactV7: Stripe direct — card fee passed through at cost
pkQuote: Every platform that started with good intentions eventually faced a board meeting where fees made sense. We wanted to make that conversation impossible.

spChannel1Body: Platform changes ship with a feedback window. The split and moderation heuristics are published for public audit — check our work.
spChannel2Body: Every DJ and promoter gets the same hosting tools, free. No tier unlocks anything — the scene decides what gets heard.
spChannel3Body: No bots, no paid manipulation, no hidden incentives. Hype is the demand signal venues book from — keep it real.
spChannel4Body: Report unsafe content, fraud, or impersonation. Every report is tracked to a resolution in the public trust & safety report.
spCommunityBody: Users of iHYPE are stakeholders, not just customers. Meaningful changes — the split, moderation rules, new fees of any kind — are put to the people who use it.

ticketPolicyPage.intro: The ticket hub should prioritize transparent pricing, serialized tickets, venue verification, and fraud prevention.
ticketPolicyPage.pricingPayoutsBody: Ticket creation should show ticket cost, capacity, tax estimates, and artist/venue/promoter payout assumptions before opening sales.
ticketPolicyPage.refundsChangesBody: Venues and event organizers are responsible for clear event-change, cancellation, refund, and reissue instructions.
ticketPolicyPage.resaleBody: Ticket resale should be limited to face value and require venue-assisted reassignment so the valid token owner is clear.
ticketPolicyPage.serializedTicketsBody: Each ticket should carry a unique ID and QR verification path so venues can validate entry once.
ticketPolicyPage.title: Verified tickets, clear event rules
tpCPIntro: iHYPE is built for independent music, which means rights handling needs to be clear and serious.
tpCPS1B: Do not upload songs, videos, artwork, samples, or logos unless you own them or have permission to use them on iHYPE.
tpCPS2B: Rights holders should report unauthorized media through the content report flow or support channel with enough detail to identify the asset.
tpCPS3B: Reported media can be hidden, removed, or restricted while iHYPE reviews ownership, license, and safety concerns.
tpCPS4B: Accounts that repeatedly upload unauthorized content may lose upload privileges or account access.
tpCRIntro: iHYPE should be useful, human, and fair. That means no harassment, fraud, manipulation, or unsafe content.
tpCRS1B: No harassment, threats, hate, doxxing, impersonation, or targeted abuse of fans, artists, venues, promoters, staff, or volunteers.
tpCRS2B: Do not use bots, fake accounts, paid manipulation, or hidden incentives to distort hype, rankings, playlists, or recommendations.
tpCRS3B: Event, ticket, safety, accessibility, and venue information should be accurate and corrected quickly when it changes.
tpCRS4B: Users should report unsafe content, rights concerns, fraud, impersonation, or ticket issues so admins can review them in the beta console.
tpCRTitle: Keep the scene safe enough to grow
tpDMIntro: To report infringing content, complete the form below. We will review and respond within 5 business days. False claims may result in account suspension.
tpDMS1B: Submit the form with your contact details, the infringing URL, and a description of your original work. We acknowledge within 48 hours. Valid claims are removed within 5 business days. The content owner is notified and may file a counter-notice.
tpDmcaNote: For DMCA takedown requests, email admin@ihype.org with subject "DMCA Takedown Request". We respond within 5 business days.
tpRequiredNote: Name, email, and infringing URL are required.
tpSubmittedMsg: Your DMCA request has been submitted. We will contact you at {email} within 48 hours.

transparencyPage.heroSub: Every dollar of ticket revenue goes directly to artists and venues. Here's the proof.
transparencyPage.reasonDataBody: iHYPE does not sell, license, or monetise listener data. Analytics are visible only to the artist or venue they belong to.
transparencyPage.reasonHypeBody: Listening to a track all the way through, or manually hyping an artist, registers a Hype. It is a demand signal — no money changes hands and iHYPE earns nothing from it.
transparencyPage.reasonRadioBody: Live and recorded radio shows are free for all hosts on the platform. There is no tier that unlocks hosting; every DJ and promoter gets the same tools.
transparencyPage.reasonTicketsBody: Tickets are sold at face value set by the artist or venue. iHYPE charges 0% on every transaction. Settlement goes directly to the organiser — only the card-processing fee (2.9% + $0.30, at cost) sits above face value.
